matchstick.title: Check arithmetic validity
matchstick.principle: After you have a candidate transformed equation, convert each Roman numeral to its integer value using standard rules and verify that the arithmetic relation holds. Without this check you may accept a syntactically valid but mathematically false equation. This prevents overlooking arithmetic errors introduced by a stick move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after forming a candidate equation from a proposed stick move.
matchstick.example: Accepting a transformed equation that still reads ‘XIX = XII + II’ without confirming that 19 ≠ 14.

matchstick.title: Match‑stick orientation matters
matchstick.principle: A stick’s orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) is fixed; you may only place it on a target character in a way that respects that orientation. Ignoring orientation creates shapes that are not valid Roman numerals or operators. This ensures every character after the move is drawable with the given sticks.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When selecting a stick to relocate and deciding where to attach it.
matchstick.example: Placing a diagonal stick on an ‘=’ sign, producing an invalid operator shape.

matchstick.title: Limit changes to two characters
matchstick.principle: The single stick move may affect only the source character (which loses the stick) and the destination character (which gains the stick); no other characters may be altered. Changing more than two characters violates the puzzle rule and leads to invalid solutions. This keeps the move strictly to one stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During the planning of a stick move.
matchstick.example: Altering both a numeral and an operator by adding sticks to each without removing any.

matchstick.title: Transform numerals via single stick moves
matchstick.principle: Only specific numeral pairs can be interconverted by moving a single stick (e.g., I↔II↔III, V↔X, L↔I, C↔L, D↔C, M↔D). The source numeral must remain a valid Roman numeral after losing the stick, and the destination must become a standard numeral. Attempting other changes creates invalid shapes.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you consider altering a numeral by moving a stick.
matchstick.example: Turning X into V by removing one diagonal, which leaves a single diagonal that is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The response must be a single line that begins with ‘Correct version of the equation:’ (case‑insensitive) and contains the corrected equation with whitespace collapsed. Any deviation (missing prefix, extra lines, wrong case) causes automatic rejection. This guarantees the scorer can extract the answer.
matchstick.example: Omitting the required prefix or adding a second line after the answer.

matchstick.title: Accurate parsing of the original equation
matchstick.principle: Record each numeral and operator exactly as they appear (including order and spacing) before attempting any transformation. Mis‑parsing can cause you to move a stick from the wrong character or mis‑interpret the equation structure. Accurate parsing is the foundation for a correct move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving the puzzle.
matchstick.example: Treating ‘XVIII’ as ‘XVII’ and moving a stick from the wrong numeral.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to a ‘‑’ creates a ‘+’; removing the vertical stick from a ‘+’ yields a ‘‑’. These are the only valid vertical‑stick transformations between operators. Using any other vertical‑stick change produces an invalid operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to change a ‘‑’ to ‘+’ or vice versa.
matchstick.example: Turning ‘‑’ into ‘×’ by adding a vertical stick, which is not an allowed operator.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick transfer from '+' to numeral (adds I)
matchstick.principle: Removing the vertical stick from a ‘+’ turns it into ‘‑’; the removed stick can be added to a numeral that needs an extra vertical stick, effectively increasing its value by one (e.g., I → II). Both source and destination must remain valid after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a numeral can be increased by one and the plus sign can afford to lose its vertical stick.
matchstick.example: Adding a vertical stick to ‘V’ to make ‘X’, which does not correspond to a simple vertical‑stick transfer.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion via horizontal stick relocation
matchstick.principle: Removing one horizontal line from ‘=’ turns it into ‘‑’; adding that horizontal line to a ‘‑’ creates ‘=’. These are the only valid horizontal‑stick transformations between operators. Any other use of a horizontal stick on an operator yields an invalid symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to swap ‘=’ with ‘‑’ or adjust the equality sign.
matchstick.example: Adding a horizontal stick to ‘+’ to make ‘=’, which is not a permitted transformation.

matchstick.title: Numeric gap assessment and operator swap priority
matchstick.principle: Compute the numeric values of both sides; if the absolute difference exceeds the maximum change achievable by a single numeral transformation (±5 for V↔X, ±2 for I↔III, etc.), prioritize moving a stick between operators (e.g., swapping ‘=’ with ‘‑’ or ‘+’ with ‘‑’) to preserve the equality sign while adjusting the arithmetic. This avoids futile numeral changes that cannot bridge a large gap.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the arithmetic discrepancy is larger than the largest possible single‑numeral change.
matchstick.example: Turning ‘XIX = XIX + XIX’ into ‘XIX - XIX + XIX’, which removes the ‘=’ sign and leaves the equation without a valid equality.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on making the symbols look correct and forgets to check whether the resulting numbers satisfy the equation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always convert each Roman numeral to its integer value after a transformation and confirm the arithmetic holds before outputting the answer.

matchstick.why_it_happens: When moving a stick, the solver may leave a numeral with an unsupported combination of sticks (e.g., a single diagonal for X).
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Refer to the allowed single‑stick numeral transformations and ensure both source and destination remain standard Roman numerals.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may add or remove sticks in a way that yields a shape that is not one of the allowed operators (+, -, =).
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Limit operator changes to the documented vertical and horizontal stick conversions; never produce a shape that does not match '+', '-', or '='.

matchstick.description: Missing destination for moved stick (effective removal)
matchstick.why_it_happens: A stick is taken from a character (often '=') and not placed onto another character, leaving the equation without an equality sign or with an incomplete operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure every stick you remove is added to a different character, preserving a valid operator in the final equation.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The final line does not start with the exact required prefix or contains extra whitespace/lines, causing the scorer to miss the answer.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Output exactly one line beginning with ‘Correct version of the equation:’ followed by the corrected equation, with no extra text.
